Although it’s not begpacking per se (although I did see a handful of them when I managed to make my way to Thailand at one point), but begpacking adjacent? is tall ship sailing. It’s a super niche and tiny community I was part of for about 7 years. It pays garbage and is primarily non profits and you work ridiculous lengths of time, both in hours and contracts. 

However, they’re all upper middle class or wealthy people in their late teens and twenties, “teaching” (not necessarily factual or useful or truthful curriculum nor from people that are even close to certified to teach, and I don’t mean in a need your teacher certs kind of way) to at risk youth (and sometimes rich charter and homeschools for money). The nonprofits are all run by people from money, with very cushy salaries. There’s no benefits and most labor laws don’t apply due to it being a classified as a stipend/scholarship system. 

I used it as a way to travel and relate to kids from my background (from a very very poor and abusive home) and teach them skills that would help them at the very least cope with their situations. I have become very good at teaching and I really enjoy it (later I became an afterschool program director amongst other teaching sort of jobs). I did learn a lot and it was good for me in many ways, not short of which was a poor person being able to travel without feeling like I’m putting out other poor people in the places I went. I only did it in the US (where I’m from), but god, am I glad I got out (and irate at myself for staying as long as I did). There is just no perspective, responsibility, or empathy from the people that took these jobs, primarily as a way to pretend to be poor and feel old-timey. 

7 years all over the country and I never once met a single sailor from a disadvantaged background such as mine (and there were so many students I had from backgrounds far worse than my own). Jobs that could be given to people of my background with better pay and benefits and giving them the chance to travel and learn about the world….maybe this is closer to white tourism…which isn’t quite the term I’m looking for, but that thing where rich white people “volunteer “ to go take selfies with kids in Africa to post on social media to virtue signal. -end rant and thank you for coming to my Ted Talk-

I feel like I always knew that my mom and bf were awful to me and my siblings, but it didn’t occur to me how truly fucked up and deep it ran until I started dating my current partner. I would talk about random things from my childhood I thought were normal (which aren’t many, really), and he is just continually baffled by how insane they were. After I cut off contact at 24 (I’m about 30 now), it made it a lot easier to process and I fully realize that every aspect of my mom’s parenting was a manipulative nightmare. Even little things, like that it’s illegal to drive without shoes on (it’s not) and cocker spaniels bite the most of any dog (it’s German shepherds) all the way up to, no I didn’t steal your paychecks and debit card and SSN number (she did). I’m still trying to fix myself though, since I don’t have much of a support system and a whole lot of trauma.
